java_model_supported: ClusterDecoration builds a Fashion with the caller's RoundCorner and passes it unchanged to symbol.asBig().

EntityImageDescription resolves explicit symbol leaves from root.element.<diagramStyle>.<symbol>.title, while EntityImageEmptyPackage resolves ordinary empty packages from root.element.<diagramStyle>.package.title.
DiagramType.CLASS maps to classDiagram and DiagramType.DESCRIPTION maps to componentDiagram before those style signatures are merged.
USymbolStack.drawQueue uses a zero-only straight polyline branch and otherwise rounds both the inset rectangle and the outer path from the resolved diameter.
rust_model_audit: class.rs introduces stack_round_corner() that always resolves root.element.classDiagram.group.stack and writes that same value into both LayoutPackageCluster.round_corner and EmptyPackageLayout.round_corner.
The class explicit-symbol and packageStyle-derived empty-package paths therefore share a cluster signature in Rust even though Java splits them across explicit-symbol and package-title signatures.

deployment.rs introduces deployment_stack_round_corner(diagram, cluster), but it resolves only diagram.meta.style_program and falls back to the hardcoded 5px default; legacy generic roundcorner skinparams never reach the deployment cluster path.
The deployment explicit leaf path still honors selector-specific style-program data, which is why the DESCRIPTION leaf perturbation passes while the DESCRIPTION cluster perturbation fails.

findings.summary: The class explicit stack leaf still resolves the wrong corner style.
findings.detail: In checker_class_leaf_selector_odd_scale, Java keeps LeafCache913 at the default 5px diameter (scaled rx/ry 3.125), while Rust rounds the same leaf to 19px (scaled rx/ry 11.875). The class wrapper frame itself stays at the default radius in both outputs, so the divergence is isolated to the explicit stack leaf branch.

findings.summary: The class packageStyle empty-package path still uses cluster-style stack corners instead of package-title corners.
findings.detail: In checker_class_packagestyle_even_dpi, Java paints the nested LedgerShelf927 empty package with large stack arcs from the package-title selector (scaled 31.5 / 21 corner geometry), while Rust keeps the same leaf on the 5px cluster-style path (scaled 6.5625 / 4.375 geometry).

findings.summary: The deployment stack cluster still ignores the generic roundcorner skinparam.
findings.detail: In checker_description_cluster_odd_scale, Java applies skinparam roundcorner 17 to the DESCRIPTION stack cluster and emits rx/ry 14.875 after scale 1.75; Rust stays on the default rx/ry 4.375, which matches the hardcoded 5px diameter rather than the requested style.

findings.summary: Two held-outs do support the narrow pieces of the account.
findings.detail: checker_class_cluster_style_after_zero and checker_description_leaf_even_dpi both compare structurally equal. Class cluster zero-corner handling and deployment explicit-leaf selector handling therefore generalize across these fresh renamed inputs.

findings.summary: No overfitting signal was found in the implementation diff.
findings.detail: The rejecting verdict comes from fresh valid inputs and source-audited dispatch gaps, not from fixture-shaped logic, comparator slack, or baseline changes.

verdict_reason: The shared stack-corner model is not complete at 2ed0e249. Fresh valid perturbations still break three distinct branches: explicit CLASS stack leaves, packageStyle-derived CLASS empty packages, and generic-roundcorner DESCRIPTION stack clusters. Under the held-out rule, any one of those failures rejects the mechanism; together they show the class and deployment consumers still do not share Java's full round-corner dispatch.
